subject: Accountancy
central_question: How are trial-balance items classified and assembled into trading and profit and loss account and balance sheet to report performance and financial position?
in_scope_units: Capital and revenue expenditure and receipts.
Meaning, nature and objectives of financial statements.
Trading account and calculation of gross profit or gross loss.
Profit and loss account and calculation of net and operating profit.
Balance sheet and classification of assets and liabilities.
Grouping and marshalling in order of liquidity or permanence.
Preparation of financial statements of a sole proprietor.
banned_topics: Adjustments such as outstanding expenses, prepaid expenses and provisions, which belong to Financial Statements – II.
Trial-balance error correction, which belongs to Chapter 6.
Company financial-statement formats, which are outside this sole-proprietor chapter.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every large payment is capital expenditure.
known_pitfalls.correction: Classification depends on purpose and benefit period, not merely amount.

known_pitfalls.claim: Purchase of goods for resale is shown as an asset purchase in the balance sheet.
known_pitfalls.correction: It enters the trading account as purchases; unsold goods become closing stock.

known_pitfalls.claim: Gross profit and net profit are the same.
known_pitfalls.correction: Gross profit arises from trading activities before indirect expenses and incomes; net profit is determined after them.

known_pitfalls.claim: A balance sheet is an account covering a period.
known_pitfalls.correction: It is a statement of financial position at a particular date.

known_pitfalls.claim: Closing stock always appears only in the balance sheet.
known_pitfalls.correction: When supplied as additional information, it is normally credited in trading account and shown as a current asset.
